module.purpose: Provides typed query expressions, recursive matching, and indexed execution for filtering records in the store.
module.summary: This module defines a recursive query language supporting equality, inequality, and numeric greater-than predicates. It flattens nested criteria into indexed property paths, gathers candidate record identifiers from reactive indexes, short-circuits impossible matches, and intersects candidate sets. A separate recursive matcher provides direct object-level validation with semantics aligned to indexed execution.
module.businessContext: Supports querying application records such as books or authors through the store layer. Failure would produce incorrect filtering or inefficient record lookup.
functions: isQueryValueMatcher (~L53-56): Identifies whether a value is a direct query matcher
extractMatcherPaths (~L58-79): Recursively flattens nested query criteria into indexed paths
objectMatchesQuery (~L81-107): Recursively checks whether an object satisfies query criteria
executeQuery (~L135-184): Retrieves and intersects indexed IDs matching a store query

preconditions: query is a query expression whose enumerable entries can be traversed with Object.entries.
postconditions: Returns one result for each traversed value recognized as a query value matcher.
Each result contains the matcher object and its path from the query root.
Nested property names are joined using a single backslash separator.
invariants: Results are emitted in the depth-first order of Object.entries traversal.
An object containing at least one of the eq, neq, or gt properties is treated as a matcher rather than recursively traversed.
The input query and matcher objects are not mutated.
edgeCases: An empty query returns an empty array.
A direct matcher is returned with its property name as the path, or with the supplied prefix before that property.
Nested query objects produce flattened paths with backslash-separated keys.
Null values and non-object, non-matcher values are ignored.
Objects containing any of eq, neq, or gt are classified as direct matchers even if they contain other properties.

detail.name: objectMatchesQuery
detail.signature: export function objectMatchesQuery<T extends object>(query: QueryExpression<T>, object: T)
preconditions: query is a query expression whose entries are query matchers or nested query expressions.
object is a non-null object compatible with T.
postconditions: Returns true only when every query entry matches the corresponding object value.
Returns false as soon as any query condition does not match.
invariants: All query entries must match; matching is conjunctive.
Nested query expressions are evaluated recursively against the corresponding nested object value.
A neq matcher never matches an undefined object value.
edgeCases: An empty query matches any object and returns true.
An eq matcher returns false when the corresponding value is not strictly equal to eq.
A neq matcher returns false when the corresponding value is strictly equal to neq or is undefined.
A gt matcher returns false unless the corresponding value is a number strictly greater than gt.
A nested query returns false when its corresponding value is null, non-object, or fails recursive matching.
When multiple matcher conditions are present, failure of any condition returns false.

errorPolicy.onInvalidInput: For a query entry requiring nested matching, a null or non-object corresponding value produces false. Inputs that are not valid objects or query expressions are outside the stated preconditions.
errorPolicy.returnsOnError: false for a non-matching or structurally invalid query entry
